title: A run's record lives in the plan and in git
description: The gate runner appends every run to an evidence ledger beside the plan, and the readers that grew on it are no longer only a cache of a verdict: the time per task, the repeat of a step whose inputs did not change, the drive's reading of a run it launched in the background, the reading of a red against the base, and the binding of a commit to the run that graded it all read ledger rows. A design that only says the ledger's writes go away would take those with it. So the record moves first, the readers follow through one seam, and the writes stop last, each step with a green gate behind it. The plan and git are the two stores that remain; a row already written stays readable as frozen history and is never migrated. The properties are written before the code: after any number of recorded runs a subject holds exactly one record, the last one printed; a run that exits 0 or 1 has its record in the shard and a record that could not be written is exit 3 naming the log, never exit 0; the pointer is derivable from the record; a decision read from the record equals the run's own output for green and red with no commit made; a recorded run changes no byte inside the content identity; a plan and ledger written by the previous release answer the same after the upgrade, and with the ledger deleted the gate conditions still answer the same. Out of scope here and next in line: the drive's own state, the filed returns, the brief protocol and the subagent writer.
desiredOutcome: A task's verdict is in its commit's Audit-Task, Audit-Gate and Audit-Run trailers, the newest run of every task and phase is one record in its own shard, a phase's CI run is in its shard, every reader of recorded runs goes through one reader over those records and the frozen older rows, the base is measured only when a red could predate the task, and no evidence row, per-call journal row or preimage file is written under the default configuration.

findings.issue: The seven install steps are written out twice, and the only thing holding them together is a comment ('a change to one is owed to the other', ci.yml:~356). Nothing compares them, so a later edit to one job (a package-name tweak, a key change) leaves the other on the old shell with every gate green. The task's own dependants named gate-parity.py's matrix rules; none covers this.
findings.resolution: Move the steps into a composite action (.github/actions/browser-install/action.yml) that both jobs call, or add a gate-parity rule that fails when the two jobs' install step lists differ. Either replaces the prose rule with a mechanism.

findings.issue: The step title 'the archive is asked only for a .deb the restored set lacks' and the log line 'not in the restored set, so fetched from the archive: $fetch' say the archive is asked for the missing .deb. The code passes $MISSING, not $fetch, to apt-get install --download-only, and apt sees only the fresh $dl directory, so on a partial set the archive is asked for the whole set plus its dependency closure and cp overwrites the restored files. The result is correct (that .deb is fetched), but the claim is narrower than the behaviour and only the miss path was exercised on a real runner. Separately, the ls check names only the packages in $MISSING, so a restored set missing a dependency-only .deb (a package apt pulled in that playwright did not name) is not detected and dpkg -i fails with an unmet dependency: a red job, not a green one.
findings.resolution: Either reword the title and log line to say the whole set is refetched when any one is absent, or install $fetch and let the dependency closure follow. Optionally verify the restored set with `dpkg-deb --info` per file, or by `dpkg -i` failing over into one refetch.

findings.issue: A poisoned or truncated cache entry is permanent. Cache keys are immutable and an exact hit is never re-saved, so a bad .deb in a saved entry makes dpkg -i fail (red) on every run of that branch until the key changes or GitHub evicts it, and the step has no path that drops a restored set it cannot install. The same holds for the partial set in finding 2: the repair is not persisted, so each later run repeats the full fetch. The entry can only come to hold a bad file if the job that saved it was green, so this is unlikely, and every outcome seen in the shell is red, not a green job without the packages. The sysdeps key also omits runner.arch, which the browser key carries; a .deb for another architecture would be refused by dpkg (red).
findings.resolution: Add a manual version token to the sysdeps key (chromium-sysdeps-v1-...) so a poisoned entry can be bypassed without a code change, include runner.arch in it, and on a dpkg -i failure fall back once to the fetch path before failing.

findings.issue: The descriptive line says 'The browser jobs' install drops from 3-9 minutes to 12-26 seconds'. The before figures are slow-mirror runs; the after figures come from two fast-mirror runs, and the pre-change install on a fast mirror was 38s (run 41322244766). The change's measured saving is the 21s to 12s (panel) and 26s to 15s (report) between the miss and hit runs, and a miss on a slow mirror costs what it cost before, minus the upgrades. The ci.yml comments say exactly this; the outcome summary does not. Also, main's push runs skip the browser jobs, so main saves no entry and the first run on a new ci/ branch misses both caches, so the hit path may be the rarer one in this repo's own practice; nothing here measures the hit rate.
findings.resolution: State in the outcome that the measured install is 12-26s on a fast mirror on both paths and that the slow-mirror saving is a hit-only saving not measured; decide separately whether a workflow_dispatch on main should seed the caches.

findings.issue: The new behaviour, a verified push to main running the browser jobs with seed true, was executed by no real run. All four logs read 'seed: false' and show seen-browser and seen-sysdeps as outcome=skipped (run2-browserpanel lines 250-253); the plan step took its 'SEED != true' early exit. So actions/cache/restore@v6 with lookup-only, the cache-hit output read by the plan step, the 'entry exists for both keys, nothing installed' branch, the 'one key missing' branch and the workflow's `seed: needs.verified.outputs.run != ''` wiring have been shown only on the uncommitted stub harness. The task's acceptance 1 asked for 'a run on the default-branch path that saves the entries'; the probes were workflow_dispatch runs on a ci/ branch, which exercise the install and the save but not the seed decision. The first real execution of the seed path will be a push to main.
findings.resolution: Before landing, push one more probe commit to a ci/ branch with `seed: true` hard-wired and the slice step skipped, and read two runs: the first must print 'seed: no entry exists for the browser key and the system packages' key' then save; the second must print 'seed: an entry exists for every key this image needs, so nothing is installed and nothing is saved' and show every later step skipped. Add a third look at a run with only one of the two keys present if a cheap way exists (a changed BROWSER_CACHE_VERSION on one key is not possible, so state that this half stays stub-only).

findings.issue: Nothing in the repository guards the action's shell besides a real CI run. I searched tracked files: no test, lint or checker names .github/actions or action.yml (git grep for 'action.yml|.github/actions|actionlint|shellcheck' over tools/tests/.claude/plugins finds nothing), gate-parity.py reads only ci.yml, and the 20-case stub harness the proofs rest on (scratchpad stubs/harness.py) is not committed. The first real run found three defects the stubs could not see (Permission denied from cp -a, the image version in the key, jc0). The failure shape is also quiet: any bug that makes the hit path throw lands in `why`, the fallback fetches from the archive, and the job stays GREEN with one ::warning:: and a cache that never helps. No gate reads that warning, so the regression the whole task exists to remove (a first run paying the archive) can return with every check green. A later change (apt flags, BROWSER_CACHE_VERSION, a new package) has only a 13-minute hosted run as feedback and nothing that notices a hit turning into a fallback.
findings.resolution: Commit the harness as tests/test_browser_install.py with the `N/M cases passed` contract: extract the `run:` bodies from action.yml by step id, run them under the stub PATH, and keep si1-si10 and the sk/sp cases (full hit asks nothing, miss, partial, dependency missing, unreadable .deb falls back once, fallback failing is red). Add one case that fails when the hit path prints the ::warning:: (the hit must not fall back). If a suite is out of scope for this task, file it as the next task and name it in the outcome; the claim that the install is guarded cannot rest on an uncommitted harness.

findings.issue: An untouched sentence this diff makes false, which the return's claim 3 dismisses as 'pre-existing inexactness about verified unchanged by this task'. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md:7699 reads 'a push to main whose commit a run already verified runs only tools/ci-verified.py'. Before this change that was exact (every other job was skipped by `needs.verified.outputs.run == ''`); after it the two browser jobs run their checkout, setup, npm ci, lookups and install on that push. The task named 'the push-to-default-branch path that skips work for a verified commit' as a dependant to answer for by name, and this document is the one that describes that path outside CONTRIBUTING.md.
findings.resolution: Change the sentence to say that such a push runs `verified` and, in the two browser jobs, the install only (seeding the caches), and correct claim 3 so it lists this line as made false by the task rather than left. The same pass should re-read tools/check-rendered-artifacts.py:1429, tools/lints/_refs.py:1915 and CLAUDE.md:314 ('every job is setup plus one verify.sh call'), which stay inexact only about `verified` and are unchanged by this diff.

findings.issue: On a push to main whose commit is verified, the browser jobs now do work that can fail: npm ci and `playwright install-deps --dry-run` run before the seed decision even when both entries exist (they are needed only to name the keys), and a miss runs apt and the Chromium download. A transient npm, apt or network failure turns that main run red for a cache it did not need. That is the failure class the `verified` job exists to remove (its own comment: re-running the same bytes 'could only add a ... intermittent the first draw did not have'). It does not skip any slice, and no gate reads main's run, so the cost is a red check on an already-verified commit, not a lost verdict.
findings.resolution: Give the two jobs `continue-on-error: ${{ needs.verified.outputs.run != '' }}` so a failed seed is visible but not red, or compute the playwright pin and image name without npm ci on the seed path. Say in ci.yml which is chosen.

findings.issue: On main a running run is never cancelled and one pending run is held; a third push replaces the pending one, which then never runs. A verified push used to finish in about half a minute; it now holds the group for the seed's duration (a hit: checkout, node, npm ci, two lookups; a miss: the full install, 2m20s on the measured fast-mirror miss and up to the install's 9m22s fetch on a slow day). A commit queued behind a seeding miss is more likely to be replaced and get no run on main.
findings.resolution: State it in the comment above browser-panel as a cost of seeding, or have the seed job take its own concurrency group (`concurrency: browser-seed`) so it does not hold ci-refs/heads/main.

findings.issue: Two statements go past what the logs show. (a) outcome.descriptive says 'a hit asks the archive for nothing on any image version of the distribution'; one cross-image restore was measured (set saved on 20261111.127.1, restored on 20261111.370.1) and the action's own header (action.yml:27-44) says an image whose installed versions the set's index cannot satisfy falls back to a fresh fetch and keeps doing so on every run. (b) outcome.technical attributes the report job's 35s after the restore to 'apt Reading package lists 18s plus dpkg Reading database about 10s'. In run2-browserreport the 'Reading package lists...' line is 20:12:41.008 and the dependency listing follows at 20:12:41.34; the 18.5s gap is between 'The following NEW packages will be installed' (20:12:41.348) and '0 upgraded, 9 newly installed' (20:12:59.923), which is not apt's index read. The panel job's same stretch took 2.6s (20:12:30.0 to 20:12:32.6), so the gap is variable and unexplained, not shown to be local.
findings.resolution: Write (a) as 'on the image versions measured' and (b) as 'an unexplained 18s between the dependency listing and the summary line, not seen in the panel job'. The committed comments already avoid both claims; only the return's wording needs the change.

tasks.title: The browser jobs' time bound is about the slice: the Chromium install is timed by step and cached, and each bound's basis is re-measured
tasks.description:
The `browser (report)` job is bounded at 19 minutes on a recorded longest run of about nine, and on three runs in one day it took 17m44s once and was cut at the bound twice, the second time with the slice's VERIFY OK printed in the same second. Two costs sit in that job and in `browser (panel)` beside it. The install step (`npm ci`, then `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`) took between six and nine minutes. The slice took over eleven where its recorded longest whole job was nine.

Measure before changing: split the install into steps that each print their own duration (the package install, the browser download, the system packages) and read one run. Then remove what can be removed: cache the browser download keyed by the pinned playwright version in the lock file, and install only the system packages the runner image lacks. A cache miss must still install and pass; a cache hit must not skip a version change. For the slice: read its per-step seconds from the run's log (verify.sh prints them) and compare with the run the `longest` line names; if a step grew, name it and the commit range in the outcome and file what you find rather than fixing a product regression inside this task.

Then re-record: each browser job's `longest` line names a run measured after this change, and its bound is two to three times that, which is the rule tools/gate-parity.py holds. Do not raise a bound to make room for a cost you did not measure.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. One dispatched run (the orchestrator dispatches it on the phase's CI branch; say in the outcome which lines to read) shows the install by step, and a second shows the cached path with its seconds.
2. `python3 tools/gate-parity.py` is green: every job's bound is backed by its `longest` line.
3. The outcome states the job's whole duration before and after, each with its run id, and what remains of the slice's growth.
4. Nothing in the slice itself is skipped, narrowed or moved to the release tier to buy time.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: tools/gate-parity.py's job bounds and its matrix rules, tools/verify.sh's slices (unchanged), CONTRIBUTING.md and CLAUDE.md where they describe CI's shape, and the release-tier jobs that share the install step.

outcome.technical: Only .github/workflows/ci.yml changed. (1) The single `npm ci && npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` step in browser (panel) and browser (report) is now seven steps, identical in both jobs: npm ci; read the playwright-core pin from package-lock.json and ImageOS/ImageVersion (exits 1 if any is missing); actions/cache@v6 on <home>/.cache/ms-playwright keyed by runner os/arch and the playwright-core version; `npx playwright install chromium`, run on a hit as well so a version change is never skipped; derive the packages `playwright install-deps --dry-run chromium` names that dpkg-query does not report installed (exits 1 if no install line or no package); actions/cache@v6 on <home>/.cache/chromium-sysdeps keyed by the image version and a hash of that list; then `apt-get update` plus `--download-only` only for a .deb the restored set lacks, followed by `dpkg -i` on the set. Only the packages the image lacks are named, so mesa is no longer upgraded. (2) Measured on head 55d48673. Run 44363694425 missed both caches: panel 17:53:48-17:59:19 = 5m31s, report 17:53:48-18:05:59 = 12m11s, install 21s and 26s, mirror fast ('Fetched 21.1 MB in 0s'/'in 1s'). Run 44366022835 hit both ('every package the image lacks is in the restored set; no archive is asked'): panel 18:06:27-18:12:04 = 5m37s, report 18:06:27-18:19:04 = 12m37s, install 12s and 15s. Before the change: report 17m44s (run 44341247041) and 17m57s (run 44270291891); runs 44318839994 and 44356971266 were cut at the bound; panel 11m36s (44341247041) and 14m49s (42283005055); install 3m25s to 9m05s in the four runs read today, nearly all of it the apt fetch (for example 32.1 MB in 8m11s at 65.4 kB/s, job 134852070227). (3) The `longest` lines now read browser-panel 5m37s and browser-report 12m37s (both run 44366022835, start and end given), and the PROVISIONAL marking is gone. The bounds are 16 (panel; allowed 11m14s-16m51s, set above the minimum to hold a slow miss) and 26 (report; minimum 25m14s). A comment says what a slow miss still costs: the fetch of the packages the image lacks, 19.1 MB in 9m22s at 34.0 kB/s in run 42283005055, about nine minutes added to either job. The two measured runs had a fast mirror, so they show no saving on a slow day; the comment says so. (4) The slice is unchanged and still the remaining pole. The report slice took 11m25s (miss) and 12m04s (hit), against 8m13s in run 41322244766, the run the old `longest` line named (its log is still readable). Growth there: interactive-check steps 1m00s -> 3m00s, one-status 47s -> 2m18s, live plan 6m18s -> 5m47s; checks per page about tripled (acme-store 200 -> 584). Source: tools/check-report-interactive.mjs, commits 03f4114d (P163.1) through 1d0e3673 (P165.5). Filed in the fault register by the orchestrator, not fixed here. The report job is now about 12.5 minutes against the ten-minute workflow budget; the panel is about 5.5. (5) The cache helps only within one branch, or across branches when main holds a saved entry. Main's push runs skip the browser jobs once a commit is verified, so main rarely saves one; seeding it is the owner's call. (6) Process note: in stage two three Edit calls were refused with 'File has not been read yet' (file state was lost on resume). A `sed -i` for the two timeout values had been sent in the same parallel batch, so it ran (30->16, 36->26); after re-reading the file, the comment edits were made with Edit. Checks: `python3 tools/gate-parity.py` exit 0; Ruby YAML parse; the shell blocks run against stubs (miss, hit, partial set, three refusals). Dependants: tools/gate-parity.py unchanged and still correct (its bound rule holds the new lines; no job added or renamed, so the matrix and job-cap rules are unaffected); tools/verify.sh slices unchanged; CONTRIBUTING.md unchanged and still correct (every job is still setup plus one verify.sh --only call); CLAUDE.md not edited and still correct for the same reason; no release-tier job shares the install (resample has none, lint's npm ci is untouched). The pgo7 failures in both probe runs are tests/test_run_test_gate.py, a separate fault, not caused by this change.
outcome.descriptive: The browser jobs' install drops from 3-9 minutes to 12-26 seconds (cached browser and only the font packages the image lacks), and their bounds are re-recorded from a post-change run; the report slice's own growth (now about 12 minutes) is the remaining long pole.

tasks.title: A task's verdict is in its commit: Audit-Task, Audit-Gate, Audit-Run and Audit-Override trailers, written by the commit verb and read back from git alone
tasks.description:
The commit verb writes the verdict it bound the commit to into the commit itself. Today a task commit carries Audit-Row (a journal nonce) and an optional Co-Authored-By; which run graded it is known only through the evidence ledger and the journal. Add: Audit-Task: <task id>; Audit-Gate: <status> <gate digest>; Audit-Run: <runId>; and, when the verb was told to commit over a verdict, Audit-Override: <the reason, verbatim>. The values come from the one place that already decides them, the verdict binding the verb asks before it commits (_verdict_binding.binding): the trailers name the run the binding bound, never another, so a commit made in the phase tree after a wave member's bytes were integrated names the run that graded the phase tree's bytes. Audit-Row stays as it is.

Reading: _commit_trail.py gains the reader, over git log alone. A commit carrying Audit-Task and no Audit-Gate reads as no verdict recorded, never as passed. A commit carrying no Audit-Task (every commit made before this release, and every commit made by hand) is not a trailer commit and its verdict is read as before. Status (_status_facts.py) and the report (_evidence_view.py) read a done task's verdict at its commit from the trailers, and say which source they read.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. A task commit made by the verb in a real git fixture carries the trailers, and `git interpret-trailers --parse` returns them.
2. In a clone of that fixture with the evidence directory removed, the reader returns the same task, status, digest and run.
3. Audit-Task without Audit-Gate reads as no verdict recorded; a status word this build does not know is reported as itself, never folded into passed or failed.
4. An override reason is carried verbatim. Decide what a reason holding a newline does by what git round-trips (a folded trailer, or a refusal naming the line) and pin it with a case; a silent truncation is the defect.
5. Status and the report render the same verdict from the trailers as from the row, on one fixture read both ways.
6. A commit made over a tree other than the one the bound run graded is refused as today; the new trailers do not weaken that refusal.
7. COMPATIBILITY.md states the four trailer names as read from this release on, and that Audit-Row and the co-author trailer are unchanged; CHANGELOG.md and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md describe what the commit now carries.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: every reader of a task commit's message or trailers - _invariants.trailer_carriers and commits_carrying, the doctor's trail checks, drive-phase.py own_commit (it finds a task's commit through Audit-Row; it must keep working unchanged), close-phase.py, integrate-task.py, tools/check-git-pipeline.py (it drives the write half against a real repository and pins message shapes), and any suite asserting an exact commit message.

tasks.title: The newest run of a task or a phase is one record in its own shard, written by the gate under the phase lock
tasks.description:
Add the record that will replace the ledger row, beside the row, changing no reader yet. After a recorded run (run-test-gate.py --record, task or phase scope) the subject in its shard carries `lastRun`: the run's id, moments and durations (startedAt, durationMs, selectionMs), status and failed list, verdictSource and reusedFrom, the reuse key, the gate digest and source, leftToPhaseGate, the tested state (head, dirty, tree key), the banners and the machine and attribution lines, and per step: name, exit, ran, outcome, failing lines up to the existing cap, the measured duration when measured here, and reusedFrom when copied. A copied step carries its source's verdict fields forward, so the record is the newest measurement of each current step and no older record is needed to read it. `testEvidence` stays the three-key pointer and is written from the record in the same write. Replace, never append.

The write. Today the pointer write is skipped when the phase lock is held, because the ledger row stands anyway. A record that is the only copy cannot be skipped: the recorder takes the phase lock with a bounded wait behind any verb's write, and a record it still could not write is exit 3 naming the log path. Never exit 0 or 1 without the record. A verb that rewrites a task (move, reopen, group sign-off's copy of a carrier's pointer, reconcile) does to `lastRun` what it does to `testEvidence`.

The launch. `--launch <token>` is stored on the record, so a caller that started the run in the background can find the record of exactly that run.

Time. The recorder appends the gate and the selection stage to the task's `timing` itself, in the same locked write, from the same figures, citing the run by id; today the drive queues them in its own state from the ledger row. The stage survives the record's replacement.

ACCEPTANCE (each a case).
1. After five recorded runs of one gate a subject holds exactly one `lastRun`, its runId is the last one printed, and the shard is no larger than after the first run.
2. Exit 0 or 1 implies the shard's record names the printed runId and status; a lock that stays held past the wait is exit 3 naming the log, and the shard is unchanged.
3. `testEvidence` equals the pointer derived from `lastRun`; delete the pointer and reconcile restores it from the record.
4. A verb's write and a background record write, interleaved in both orders, both land: neither field is lost.
5. A recorded run changes no byte inside the content identity: the reuse key is the same before and after, and the set of paths the run modified (git status in a fixture) is exactly what recorded_paths names.
6. The record's size is bounded by the gate's width: failing lines per step at the existing cap, steps no more than declared plus derived. Print the measured bytes for this repository's own task gate in the outcome.
7. The schema accepts `lastRun` on a task and on a phase, a plan without it validates unchanged, and a one-file plan and a per-phase plan both carry it.
8. A machine path in a failing line reads scrubbed, as every string the shard write passes does, and the verdict fields are untouched.
9. The evidence row is still written, byte for byte as before, with the same runId as the record.

tasks.title: The base is measured only when a red could predate the task, its verdict is kept per commit, and the writer is not held for it
tasks.description:
After a red task gate the drive measures the phase's base so that a red the base already has is not blamed on the task. Today that measurement is due whenever the reading is no-base or not-knowable, the red's decision is held until the base verdict exists, and the verdict lives in a base-scope ledger row, a progress record under the drive's state and a mark. State the rule as a property of the records and move the verdict where it survives.

Needed means all three: the task gate is red; some failing case or step is not one a file this task's `tests.add` created (a case the task itself added cannot predate it); and no clean-tree measurement of that step at that base commit is recorded. Otherwise no base run is started and the decision says which of the three made it unnecessary.

Kept means: the base verdict for a commit is in the plan (on the red task's record, keyed by the base commit, readable through the one reader), computed at most once per commit and step set, and a second red at the same base reads it.

Not held means: when a writer session exists to resume, the red's failing lines go to it at once, and the base runs beside it; if the base then shows the same red, the next decision says so and the writer is not resumed over it again. Where no session exists (the dispatched writer), the decision is offered with the base named as still running rather than withheld.

Keep what the phase before this one fixed: one liveness reading decides both the reading of a base run's record and the removal of its tree.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. A red whose failing cases all live in files the task's tests.add created starts no base run, and the decision says why.

3. A red with a session to resume sends the failing lines before the base verdict exists; a base that then shows the same red produces the base decision and no further resume over that red.
4. A base run killed mid-way leaves no tree and no claim behind after the next call, as today.

tasks.title: A branch's first CI run restores the browser install: the default branch seeds the cache, the install is written once, a partial set fetches what it names and a bad entry heals
tasks.description:
The browser jobs now restore the Chromium download and the system packages the runner image lacks from a cache, and the first measurement shows what that buys and what it does not. A cache entry is saved only by a job that succeeded, and an entry is readable by the branch that saved it and by branches cut from the default branch's entries. The default branch's push runs skip the browser jobs when the commit is already verified, so the default branch saves no entry, and every phase's CI branch misses both caches on its first run. On a miss the archive is asked for about as many megabytes as before the change (the package index plus the font packages), so on a day the runner's mirror is slow the first run of a branch still pays minutes; the two runs measured so far had a fast mirror and differ by seconds. The review of that change also found three things in its shell.

Make a hit the ordinary case, and make the steps do what their names say:
1. Seed. The default branch holds a saved entry for both keys after any push that changes a key's inputs (the playwright pin in the lock file, the runner image version, the list of packages the image lacks), so a branch's first run restores it. Do it with the least new machinery that is honest: a job that runs only the install steps and saves the caches, on the default branch, when no entry for the key exists. It carries a time bound and a `longest` line like every job, and tools/gate-parity.py's rules must hold it (a job outside the slices: say how the parity rules read it, and extend them if they cannot).
2. One install, written once. The two browser jobs and the seeding job run the same steps; today the block is written out twice with a comment asking that both be changed together. Put it in one place the three jobs call (a composite action under .github/actions/ is the established form), or hold the copies to one text with a gate-parity rule that names a difference. A prose rule is not enough.
3. A partial set fetches what it names. When some but not all packages are in the restored set, the step downloads the missing ones and their dependencies and nothing else, and the check that decides a package is present covers the dependencies the install needs, not only the packages named. The step's title and log line say what the code does.
4. A bad entry heals. The system-packages key carries the runner's architecture as the browser key does. When installing from a restored set fails, the step falls back once to fetching from the archive and says so; a job is red only when that also fails. A manual version token in the key lets an operator retire an entry.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. The orchestrator dispatches runs for you as before (hand back READY-FOR-RUN with what to read, do not file): a run on the default-branch path that saves the entries, and a first run of a fresh branch that restores both. State what each line of each log must show.
2. Proven on stubs in your outcome, as the first change was: a full hit, a miss, a partial set (one package missing, one dependency missing), a restored set with a truncated package (the fallback runs once and the step passes), and the fallback failing (the step is red).
3. `python3 tools/gate-parity.py` is green and each job's bound is backed by its `longest` line; the seeding job's line names a measured run.
4. No slice is skipped, narrowed or moved; the release tier's jobs are unchanged.
5. The outcome says what a branch's first run costs after the change on a slow mirror, with the basis, and what it cost before.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: tools/gate-parity.py's job-bound, slice and matrix rules, tools/verify.sh's slices (unchanged), CONTRIBUTING.md and CLAUDE.md where they describe CI's shape (CLAUDE.md is outside this task's files: say what sentence there, if any, is no longer exact), and the push-to-default-branch path that skips work for a verified commit.

One case of tests/test__commit_trail.py, vt8, is red on Windows CI and green everywhere else: it failed in "selftests (windows, plain 2)" in both runs that carried the verdict-trailers commit (44379408461 and 44380971983), with "FAIL vt8 a FOLDED trailer reads as git unfolds it - the line break and its indent become one space - which is why the writer refuses a reason holding a line break rather than folding it: 'first half' / ['first half']". So on that runner the reader returned only the first line of a folded trailer value, where the case expects git's unfolded value. The reader asks git for `%(trailers:only,unfold)`; what differs on Windows is not established: the git version on the runner image, a carriage return in the commit message the fixture writes (a `\r\n` line end makes the continuation line something other than a folded line), or how the fixture hands the message to git there.

This matters beyond the case: the product's reader of a commit's verdict must read the same value on every platform a plan is driven on, and a reason that the WRITER refuses to fold can still arrive folded from a commit written by hand or by another tool.

Do this in order. First establish the cause with evidence, without a Windows machine: read the failing job's log for the git version (read-only gh calls on those two runs), read how the fixture writes the message (text mode, newline translation, `-F` file against `-m`), and reproduce the Windows shape here by writing the same bytes Windows would write (a `\r\n` message through `git commit -F`, and `core.autocrlf` as the runner sets it) and reading it back with the reader. Second, fix where the cause is: if the reader must tolerate a carriage return in a trailer block, it does so for every trailer it reads and not only the reason; if the fixture is what differs, the fixture writes bytes; if the runner's git does not support the unfold option the reader asks for, the reader says so as a reason it could not read, rather than returning half a value. Third, a case that is red here, on this platform, for the cause you found (the reproduction above), so the next regression does not need a Windows runner to be seen.
